analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/reference/configuration.md, lines 950-1590, a documentation-only file. The PR bumps the date and rewrites the "Cluster runtime facts" section (head ~923-1015). The truncated patch excerpt suggests the new text says a signed release can register `cluster_runtime` in its `POST /v1/releases` payload, and that a coordinator accepting the block derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it.

I saw no code change, so there is no concrete regression. The documented shift is a trust-model one. Pair approvals could previously only come from an operator-curated approval file. They may now come from release registration, which relates to A-005 (coordinator_release_api_key), A-011 (binary hash registry), A-017 (durable build qualifications) and T-054 (unqualified build accepted through stale evidence). The coordinator-side derivation is platform-owned and outside the supplied evidence. I cannot tell whether release publication alone can grant public pair serving, or whether independent qualification is still required. The base doc says the coordinator decides public serving via public cluster routing and a parity qualification, which suggests the control is retained.

The BASE units cover the approval fetch (HTTPS only, no redirect, 512 KiB cap, strict field validation), local digest checks on each Mac, link setup and isolation (osascript admin prompt, fixed commands, validated interface names) and the cluster console. These are unchanged context that the PR docs do not modify in the visible excerpts. The head text and the full patch were not available, so I could not check the changed ranges 965-1002 and 1005-1015 line by line. The threat model may need an update, covering TB-011/T-054 and the release-lane derivation of cluster approvals, if that behavior ships. That is a documentation observation, not a finding.
